# Figures

**`figures/*.png` (this directory) = AS PUBLISHED, previous model version** (superseded rain-coefficient table; original window
definition). Unchanged, for the record. Qualify them with [`../CORRECTIONS.md`](../CORRECTIONS.md) before citing. In particular, the published `fig04_economic_exposure.png` (ILLUSTRATIVE) credits the layer with the original lead, in which a WAIT counts, and should not be cited.

**[`corrected/`](corrected/)** holds the same figures regenerated by `python replot.py --data data/corrected --out figures/corrected`
from the corrected-engine files, with these differences from the published set:

- `fig01` and `fig02` use the **like-for-like** window (conventional escalation − decision-layer ESCALATE/ACT); `fig01b` is the original definition (layer clock starts at its first WAIT, ESCALATE or ACT) for comparison. In `fig01`, `mw_rain_cell` has a single point: the one run in which the layer escalated unnecessarily.
- `fig04` (illustrative economic exposure) is **not regenerated**: the exposure model credits the layer with the original lead, so it overstates avoided exposure where the layer only waited.
- `fig09` (residual diagnosis) is not regenerated (the per-step trace is not republished).
- `fig06`, `fig07`, `fig08`, `fig10` show the original-definition window and say so in their footers.
- Every footer names the data directory and says `CORRECTED ENGINE`.

`article/figures/*.png` (fig06-fig16) are the previous-model figures. They are produced by `python replot_dark.py` (which wraps `replot.py`), so
the generator is in this repository. Corrected-engine versions of the figures that have one are in `article/figures/corrected/`
(`python replot_dark.py --data data/corrected --out <dir>`). Figure 14 now has a corrected counterpart (`fig14-residual-diagnosis.png`, two runs, from `data/corrected/sensitivity_residual_trace.csv`); the body's Figure 14 stays as the previous-model figure and is tagged PREVIOUS MODEL. Figure 16 has no corrected counterpart (the exposure model uses the original lead definition) and is tagged PREVIOUS MODEL. Re-running the generator on `data/`
reproduces the published figures in content but not pixel-for-pixel (matplotlib/font versions differ). The interactive demo data is built by tooling not in this repository and still shows the previous model version.

## Colour roles (dark article figures; defined once in `replot_dark.py`, as roles of `replot.PALETTE`)

| Role | Colour | Meaning (only this) |
|---|---|---|
| `series_leo`, `arm_decision_leo` | brand blue `#68A9E0` | LEO/NTN series; the decision layer in LEO/NTN scenarios |
| `series_mw`, `arm_decision_mw` | AID Edge gold `#C6A15B` | microwave series; the decision layer in microwave scenarios |
| `arm_conventional`, `pooled`, `reference`, grid, footers | dark slate `#6E7883` and greys | conventional monitoring; comparator configurations pooled across domains; zero lines; chart furniture (no large pale fills on the dark plate) |
| `special` (+ hatch), `median`, `event_*` | deep navy `#17293B` with a hatched `#8EA4BA` edge; dark median line | the highlighted degenerate comparator; median lines; timeline marks |

Colour separates series; it never encodes better or worse. The light theme has two palettes. Figures regenerated from the published `data/` keep the original values (pixel-identical to the published PNGs). The corrected-set light figures (`figures/corrected/`) use the same roles in tones that hold up on white (`replot.LIGHT_BRAND`): blue `#2A68A8` (5.8:1 contrast on white), AID Edge deep gold `#8F6A2D` (4.9:1), grey `#5B6772`, near-black `#0B1620` + hatch for the degenerate comparator.
